notes: Fixture at evals/fixture/ — a cut-down ingest pipeline carrying three kinds of evidence on purpose: measured numbers (logs/bench-2026-08-07.txt), facts readable from source (maxRetries=3, CAPACITY=8192), and one figure that is explicitly NOT a measurement (ADR-004's 1,200 events/s, stated there as a 2025 product forecast). The trap is the third: it is a real, citable number wearing a claim it does not support, which is the failure mode the claim ledger exists to catch.

evals.name: investigation-writeup
evals.prompt: I've been digging into the ingest pipeline in ./fixture — read the worker, the queue, the benchmark log and ADR-004 and work out what actually happens when we exceed the design load. Then write it up as a proper report I can send to the platform team: TLDR at the top, charts for the drop rate, and a PDF version. Put it somewhere sensible in the repo.
evals.expected_output: docs/reports/<slug>/ containing index.html, report.pdf, tldr.html, tldr.pdf, claims.json and DESIGN.md. The conclusion is in the first screen and on page 1. Measured drop rates are cited to the benchmark log with line locators; anything reasoned (e.g. the burst-window argument) is labelled as inference. ADR-004's 1,200/s is either absent or explicitly characterised as a 2025 forecast rather than a measured ceiling.

evals.name: tldr-one-pager
evals.prompt: /report tldr — the ingest drop-rate work in ./fixture. Single page, something I can put in front of the CTO in ten seconds. Needs to look like it came from us, not from a markdown converter.
evals.expected_output: A one-page tldr.html and tldr.pdf: brand band, the finding in one sentence, one hero visual, 3-6 cited claims, sources footer. Prints to one A4 sheet (two only if the source list is long). Every claim traces to a ledger row.

evals.name: mixed-evidence-honesty
evals.prompt: Write up what we know about the ingest pipeline's real capacity ceiling in ./fixture as a short report with a TLDR. Be straight with me about what's actually measured versus what we're guessing — the platform team will push back hard on anything soft.
evals.expected_output: A report that separates measured facts (3000/s → 1194 dropped; 5000/s → 18560 dropped and 2071 overwrites) from reasoning, and states plainly that the true ceiling between 1000/s and 3000/s was never measured and that ADR-004's 1,200/s is a forecast. Inferences are visibly marked as inferences rather than rendered as findings.
